problem:
Which of the following could be matrices of quadratic forms defined on ${R}^{2}?$

$$
K=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,L=[\begin{aligned}2 & 7 \\ 7 & 0\end{aligned}],\,M=[\begin{aligned}5 & 3 \\ 6 & 6\end{aligned}]
$$

feedback.problem:
Which of the following could be matrices of quadratic forms defined on ${R}^{3}?$

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}],\,S=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 4 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 \\ 4 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,T=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 3 & -2 \\ -1 & -2 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that every quadratic form defined on ${R}^{3}$ has an associated $3\times 3$ symmetric matrix.

With that in mind, let's examine each matrix in turn.

- $R$ *cannot* be a matrix of a quadratic form defined on ${R}^{3}$ since it's a $2\times 2$ matrix (not $3\times 3$).

- $S$ *cannot* be a matrix of a quadratic form defined on ${R}^{3}.$ Although it's a $3\times 3$ matrix, $S$ is not symmetric since ${s}_{23}\ne {s}_{32}.$

- $T$ could be a matrix of a quadratic form defined on ${R}^{3}$ since it is a $3\times 3$ symmetric matrix.

Therefore, the correct answer is "$T$ only."
